events.summary: District Judge Seamus P. Duffy denied Todd Thompson's motion to dismiss cannabis charges, ruling that Minnesota retains authority to prosecute cannabis offenses on White Earth Band reservation land despite the state's legalization of adult-use cannabis. events.title: Trump administration discussed military strike on Houthis via unsecure Signal app
events.summary: On March 24, Jeffrey Goldberg of The Atlantic reported that senior Trump administration officials, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, discussed a military strike on Houthis in Yemen using an unsecure commercial Signal messaging app. Hegseth posted precise details of munitions and aircraft involved. The app was configured to auto-delete messages in violation of the Presidential Records Act. Neither President Trump nor the acting Joint Chiefs chairman was included; White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller apparently made the strike decision based on his interpretation of Trump's wishes. The White House declared the matter "closed" on March 31 without investigation or resignations.
events.why_relevant: Circumventing secure communications protocols and the Presidential Records Act for military decisions undermines national security oversight and constitutional accountability for war decisions.

In violation of the Presidential Records Act, the app was set to delete the messages.

events.title: Supreme Court denies certiorari in Franklin v. New York; Justices Alito and Gorsuch issue statements criticizing Confrontation Clause jurisprudence
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied a petition for certiorari in Franklin v. New York (No. 24–330), a case involving the admissibility of a bail report at trial without cross-examination of its author. Justice Alito issued a statement arguing that Crawford v. Washington's interpretation of the Confrontation Clause should be reconsidered, citing subsequent scholarship that undermines Crawford's historical foundations and noting the doctrine's unpredictable results. Justice Gorsuch issued a separate statement criticizing the "primary-purpose test" for determining whether statements are "testimonial" under the Sixth Amendment, arguing the test lacks textual or originalist grounding and has produced inconsistent formulations across cases.
events.why_relevant: The statements signal potential future reconsideration of foundational Sixth Amendment doctrine governing criminal defendants' right to confront witnesses, with two Justices expressing deep skepticism of settled precedent.
events.basis: The petition for a writ of certiorari is denied. Statement of JUSTICE ALITO respecting the denial of certiorari. I agree that we should not grant certiorari in this case, but in an appropriate case we should reconsider the interpretation of the Confrontation Clause that the Court adopted in Crawford v. Washington.

events.summary: Rümeysa Öztürk, a 30-year-old Fulbright scholar and doctoral student at Tufts University, was detained by masked plainclothes ICE officers on Tuesday in a Boston suburb. events.title: FTC commissioners file lawsuit challenging Trump terminations
events.summary: Democratic FTC commissioners Rebecca Kelly Slaughter and Alvaro Bedoya filed a lawsuit on March 28, 2025, challenging their terminations by President Trump announced the previous week. They argue the removals violated the FTC Act, which permits removal only for inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance, and violated the First and Fifth Amendments. The complaint seeks a court declaration that the terminations are unlawful and that the commissioners be reinstated to serve their remaining terms. Trump's removal notice cited only inconsistency with administration priorities, not statutory grounds.
events.why_relevant: The lawsuit directly challenges presidential removal authority and statutory protections for independent agency commissioners, raising fundamental questions about separation of powers and the rule of law.
events.basis: Two Democratic commissioners fired by Donald Trump from the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) filed a lawsuit on Thursday to challenge their 'indefensible' terminations.

events.why_relevant: The President's non-committal response to ongoing attacks on civilians in a U.S.-aligned nation signals a potential shift in U.S. commitment to Ukrainian defense and raises questions about the prioritization of the conflict.
events.basis: Trump was asked today whey he wasn't doing anything to stop the daily drone attacks by the Russia against Ukrainian civilians: 'Well, we're gonna see what happens with that. I'm getting reports on that. I have that high on my list of things to watch.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Flight 2983 and US Air Force T-38 jets receive collision-avoidance instructions at Reagan National Airport
events.summary: On Friday, 28 March, Delta Air Lines Flight 2983 (Airbus A319 with 136 people aboard) was cleared for takeoff at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport at approximately 3:15 p.m. while four US Air Force T-38 Talon jets were simultaneously inbound for an Arlington National Cemetery flyover. An onboard alert notified the Delta flight crew of nearby aircraft. Air traffic controllers issued corrective diversion instructions to both the commercial flight and the military jets to prevent collision. The incident occurred roughly two months after a 29 January crash at the same airport killed all 67 people aboard a passenger jet and US Army helicopter, which had prompted federal investigators to recommend restricting certain helicopter operations in the area.
events.why_relevant: The near-miss reveals ongoing airspace coordination failures at a major airport following a fatal collision, raising questions about whether prior safety recommendations were adequately implemented and whether civil-military air traffic protocols are sufficient to prevent loss of life.
events.basis: Delta Air Lines Flight 2983 was cleared for takeoff at the Reagan airport at about 3.15pm, at the same time four US air force T-38 Talon aircraft were inbound… Air traffic controllers 'issued corrective instructions to both aircraft'.

events.title: Five senior CDC officials depart following Trump administration pressure
events.summary: Five senior officials departed the CDC the day after Trump's announcement of Monarez's appointment, including the heads of the Office of Science, the Public Health Infrastructure Center, and the National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, as well as communications director Kevin Griffis. The departures occurred amid Trump and Elon Musk's broader assault on federal agencies, signaling potential institutional degradation at the CDC.
events.why_relevant: The rapid exodus of senior scientific and administrative leadership from the CDC undermines the agency's capacity to function as an independent, science-driven institution and suggests political purging of career professionals.
